chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Dirraj, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man bought the straw of a haystack, each kur for a known amount, so he takes possession of the straw and sells it before the grain is measured. He said: 'There is no objection.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no objection / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell the straw of a haystack before measuring the grain inside it?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the sale of straw (*tibn*) from a haystack (*bidr*) independently of the grain, even when possession (*qabd*) occurs before the grain is weighed. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Islamic commercial law regarding the separation of components within a single storage unit, provided the specific item sold is clearly identified and possessed. It underscores the principle that partial ownership and sale are permissible as long as the subject matter is distinct and free from excessive uncertainty (*gharar*).
